**Priority at 88, 126 and 199, and a correction to the issue text.**

My prior-art check looked only at the per-case `minimal_polynomial` fields and the atlas exact-form table, and missed T-193 in `RESULTS.md`. The sides I gave at 88, 126 and 199 are Evan Daniel's, reported in #639 on 16 October and registered as T-193 with exact configurations. My values there are a second, independent derivation of known results, and the credit for them is his.

This makes one paragraph of the issue text wrong. It says that 15/2 + 3√2 lies "about 1.2·10⁻²²" below the verified rational bound at 126, and that an exact certificate would tighten the verified bound. The gap to that rational bound is in fact 1.17·10⁻¹⁹, but the comparison is moot: T-193 already verifies the side 15/2 + 3√2 with an exact configuration. Please disregard that paragraph.

Thank you for registering 172 and 263 as T-244. I will try to supply exact configurations at those two counts, with every centre and half-angle tangent in a number field containing the side, so that the entry can be checked rather than only recorded.

Exact configurations for T-244 (n = 172 and 263).

Claim. The T-244 sides are now realized by exact configurations: s(172) ≤ S*₁₇₂ and s(263) ≤ S*₂₆₃, with S* the roots of P₁₇₂ (degree 24) and P₂₆₃ (degree 17) given in this issue. In each configuration every centre and every half-angle tangent lies in a number field K, the side S* lies in K, every contact is an identity in K, and every other pair and every wall is separated exactly.

n | K | configuration vs the record (T-174's witness, atlas best-.json at 659ee62) -- | -- | -- 172 | degree 24, generated by the half-angle tangent of the 44.73° band | centres within 1.8·10⁻¹², angles within 6.5·10⁻¹²° 263 | degree 17, generated by the half-angle tangent of the 43.81° band | centres within 3.5·10⁻¹³, angles within 3.3·10⁻¹²°

These are the records' own arrangements, not new packings.

Certificate. The attached t244-exact-configurations.zip has SHA-256 16e6ad9d04f1def897478e59260880320bc7c06ae89e41fa83837c7dc29c9a2d. It contains:

  • n172.minpoly.json, SHA-256 9230aa7aa4c6d4f4e31de4543b87e19db1e57bf4f8e105974c8bd45b203f02db
  • n263.minpoly.json, SHA-256 de646870e0ecd0d6c042e4742de023ebbcdddb28aac4aa51469dbf53dc264686

Both are in exactly the minpoly.json format of evand/square-packing search/exact/verify_exact.py, the checker reviewed for T-193. The zip also contains an independent checker, the controls, a distance script, a README and SHA256SUMS.

[t244-exact-configurations.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33922338/t244-exact-configurations.zip)

Checking.

  1. verify_exact.py, run unchanged from evand/square-packing at 659ee62e4a9d39542a1146e8b011cc3ab6407ede:

    • n172.minpoly.json: VALID … field degree 24; 1026 touching incidences proved as identities in K, 4030 strict by intervals, 14130 pairs by discs
    • n263.minpoly.json: VALID … field degree 17; 1593 touching incidences proved as identities in K, 6231 strict by intervals, 33549 pairs by discs

  2. check_field_packing.py, from the zip:

    • n = 172: VALID, 347 contacts exact in K, 683 strict by Arb balls.
    • n = 263: VALID, 564 contacts exact in K, 1043 strict by Arb balls.

    It shares no code with verify_exact.py. Its arithmetic is FLINT fmpq_poly mod f, with signs from Arb balls after exact bisection of the t interval. Its separation test is projection on the side normals, not corners against side lines. It also checks that f is irreducible and that the number of squares equals n.

Each checker runs in under 10 seconds per file.

Controls. controls.py mutates a certificate and reruns a checker. Both checkers reject, at both counts:

  • a duplicated square with n raised;
  • the side reduced by 10⁻³⁰;
  • the t interval moved off the root;
  • a band square turned by about 10⁻³⁰;
  • single-square moves by 10⁻³⁰.

The only accepted moves are two directions of square 0 at 263, where it has slack, and both checkers accept those identically. verify_exact.py reads only the first n squares, so a file with an extra square but unchanged n passes it. The claim is about the first n squares, so this does not affect soundness.

How they were built.

  1. From the 3000-digit KKT solution, recognize the band's half-angle tangent t, its minimal polynomial f, S and every other angle in Q(t) by LLL. Every angle lies in K. Squares whose angle is a free direction were snapped back to their class (drift ≤ 2·10⁻¹⁶).
  2. With the angles and S exact, the contacts are linear in the centres. Pin that system's free directions to the record's binary64 values exactly: 8 coordinates at 172 and 3 at 263.
  3. Solve the linear system to about 2850 digits and recognize every centre in Q(t).

Neither checker depends on these steps.

What the checkers share. The input files. Also, check_field_packing.py was written in the same session and with the same AI assistance as the certificates.

Not done. No Lean formalization. As before, these are upper bounds, not optimality claims.

AI assistance. The construction, the second checker and the controls were produced by Claude (Anthropic, model Claude Opus 5.5) at my direction; I reviewed and reran them.
